newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle steady $63, thin - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle steady $63, thin - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade on Friday was light at $63.00 per cwt, steady with sales this week and down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.

An estimated 200 steers sold in Kansas. Weekly sales were pegged near 95,000 head, the sources said. Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots reported no trades on Friday following a weekly movement estimated at 104,600 head.

Most showlists this week were sold out as feedlots worked to remain current, they said. Packers reportedly bought enough live inventory to get through next week's holiday-shortened schedule. U.S. Independence Day is Friday, July 4.
Cattle owners next week were seen pricing cattle at $64.00 amid outlooks for packer buying at midweek for post-holiday operations, the feedlot sources said.
However, prices could be pressured by projections for larger supplies of market-ready cattle coming in just as retail demand was seen tapering off, they said.

One uncertain factor was the weather. Forecasters next week expect a dome of hot air to establish itself over the southern plains, which could last until mid-July and ignite temperature extremes in the upper 90s and 100s-plus Fahrenheit from central Texas into western Kansas.
